Zig Ziglar once told Kevin Trudeau he could beat the world's greatest archer in a match, every single time.

Kevin's reaction: that's impossible, the guy's an Olympian. Ziglar's answer: it's simple. Blindfold him.

How's he supposed to hit a target he can't see? Exactly, Ziglar said. Most people live their whole life trying to hit a target they don't even have.

Kevin ties it back to Napoleon Hill's Think and Grow Rich: the entire key to success comes down to one thing - define your dream, and get a burning desire for its achievement. Everything else is details.

What's the target you haven't actually named yet?

#kevintrudeau #successhabits #mindset #goalsetting #motivation #entrepreneur

One rule. The richest man alive, at the time, said it mattered more than anything else.

Aristotle Onassis - the Greek shipping magnate who later married Jackie Kennedy - said the single most important factor in success is who you associate with. Associate with losers, you become a loser. Associate with winners, it rubs off.

Kevin Trudeau says his own mother used to get furious at him as a kid for listening to motivational tapes by self-made millionaires. "Keep listening to those people," she'd warn, "and you're going to turn out just like them."

His response: that's the point.

Who have you been letting rub off on you?

#kevintrudeau #successhabits #wealthmindset #mindset #entrepreneur #motivation

When he was in Austria, skinny as a rail, Arnold Schwarzenegger taped pictures of bodybuilders to the wall next to his bed - the exact physique he wanted to build. His mother was more comfortable with the other boys' pinups of girls.

But the pictures weren't the real technique. Every night before sleep, he closed his eyes and saw himself on stage, winning Mr. Olympia - the trophy in his hands, the crowd applauding, flexing under the lights. He held that image, vividly, night after night.

Years later, when it actually happened, he said the real moment was almost identical to the one he'd been picturing since he was a kid.

#kevintrudeau #mindset #visualization #successhabits #motivation #wealthmindset

Kevin Trudeau was sitting on a porch in Macon, Georgia, sipping iced tea, when an old hound dog lying nearby kept letting out a little howl, putting its head back down, then howling again a few minutes later.

"What's wrong with your dog?" he asked. "Oh," his friend said, "he's sleeping on a nail." "Why doesn't he move, then?" Kevin asked.

"It doesn't hurt him that much."

That's most people's entire relationship with the thing holding them back. Not painful enough to actually get up and move - just painful enough to howl about it every few minutes, for years.

What nail are you still lying on?

#kevintrudeau #mindset #successhabits #motivation #personalgrowth #selfimprovement

I meet this gal - blonde, blue-eyed, a cheerleader for an NFL team, Kevin Trudeau says. He asked her to dinner Friday, said he'd pick her up at seven, told her to dress nice because he would be.

The next morning, she told him what actually got her attention that night. It wasn't the restaurant or the sport coat.

It was that he never once asked what food she liked or where she wanted to go. He just decided, and took her. "Guys don't do that anymore," she told him. "You took charge without being controlling. That's what made you a man."

Decisive isn't the same as controlling. Most guys never learn the difference.

#kevintrudeau #relationshipadvice #mindset #masculinity #datingtips #selfimprovement

Ken Norton was heavyweight champion of the world. He's one of the only men who ever beat Muhammad Ali. He started with nothing and built success in business long after boxing.

Kevin Trudeau says that every single time he shakes Ken Norton's hand, Norton says the same thing, like a greeting: "Whatever the mind of man can conceive and bring itself to believe, it can achieve." Napoleon Hill's words, repeated so many times they became how Norton says hello.

Kevin's advice to any man listening is the same line: go for your dreams, and don't let anyone steal them.
